hints: Focus on what is left after the acid loses its acidic hydrogens, that tells you the charge on the anion.
Remember aluminium is in Group 13, so it forms an $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ion, while the ethanedioate ion from a diprotic acid is $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$.
Balance the total positive and negative charges to zero to find how many of each ion you need in the neutral salt.
walkthrough:
**Find the charge on the ethanedioate ion**

Think of the acid as two carboxylic acid groups joined together. Each $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ can lose one $\text{H}^+$.

$$\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+$$
So ethanedioate is a 2- ion.

**Recall the charge on aluminium**

Aluminium is a Group 13 metal and always forms the same simple ion in its salts. It loses three electrons.

$$\text{Al} \rightarrow \text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^-$$

**Balance charges to make a neutral compound**

We need total + charge = total - charge. The lowest common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6.

$$2 \times (+3) + 3 \times (-2) = 0$$
So we need 2 $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions and 3 $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions, giving $\text{Al}_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3$.

options.A: This suggests a 1 to 1 combination of $\text{Al}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$. That would only balance if aluminium were 2+, but aluminium is $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and ethanedioate is 2-, so the charges do not cancel.
options.B: This uses one $\text{Al}^{3+}$ with three $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions. The total charge would be (+3) + 3(-2) = -3, not neutral. This is the trap of copying the 3 from aluminium without balancing properly.
options.C: This has two aluminiums but only one ethanedioate unit and no brackets. The charge would be 2(+3) + (-2) = +4, far from neutral, and it ignores that the whole $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$ group must be multiplied by 3.
options.D: Two $\text{Al}^{3+}$ ions give +6 and three $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ ions give -6, so the compound is neutral. The brackets correctly show three whole ethanedioate ions: $\text{Al}_2(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3$.
